Basic Information for CVE-2026-67319 Vulnerability Information axios before 0.33.0 Prototype Pollution via nested option objects Overview This vulnerability affects the Axios library, which fails to properly check whether a property is an own property when handling nested request option objects. As a result, if the Object.prototype of the JavaScript process is polluted by other components, inherited properties may be read. Although the top-level merged configuration uses a null prototype, nested plain objects such as auth and paramsSerializer are cloned as plain objects and read, leading to potential security risks. Affected Versions Axios 0.x: Versions below 0.33.0 Axios 1.x: Versions below 1.18.0 Details Root Cause: Nested plain objects (e.g., auth, paramsSerializer) are not checked for own properties after cloning, resulting in direct reading of properties from the prototype chain. Trigger Condition: Pre-existing prototype pollution must be present, meaning Object.prototype has already been polluted by other components. Specific Manifestations: If an application passes placeholder nested objects (e.g., auth: {}), inherited username or password properties may cause silent injection of the Authorization: Basic header. Inherited encode or serialize properties may alter the serialization behavior of query strings (note: completely replacing the serializer requires prototype pollution with a function-typed primitive).
